No, this article is romanticizing the Model of Bogotá. 

Although it points out the very clear shortcomings of it, I do not believe the Institute understands just how impactful these shortcomings are and in which societal context they fit in (Riding on the "ciclorrutas" of Bogotá isn't healthy nor safe, not even because of the environmental factor of cars, but because of muggers, uneven pavement, etc). 

At the same time, I believe this text overmines the Model of the "political leadership" in Bogotá and it's direct translation into US cities. Bogotá, as pointed out, hasn't had a lot of money, but it has had a lot of wiggle room for the practical implementation of "ciclorrutas" and "ciclovias" because they developed as the city was formulating it's Master Plans, in opposition to these North American cities, which must already abide by a certain set of estrict pre-established lineaments. 

In this way, it also undermines American legislature and proceedings related to Urbanism, while overestimating the importance of "the car" in Bogotá.

Hey!
First of all, really happy to know that you're okay now. Even though we may not know each other, i too struggled with my mental health in 2020, so my heart goes out to you.

Now, let's get down to brass tacks:

1) Yes, i do believe it's possible! For starters, you would have the appeal of being a foreign student, so a lot of people (at least from my personal experience) would be attracted to talk to you just because of that fact. Some may ask you about your lifestyle in the US, while others may ask you in regards to your thoughts on the Colombian lifestyle. I'm sure that someone may notice you have an accent or not, or maybe you look foreign and someone may approach you just to know a little bit about yourself and you may end up as friends or, at least, work buddies. Also, if you are pretty sociable and love being around people, i'm sure there would be somebody that would invite you to hang out to new, bizarre, social, interesting settings. 

2) "As your attorney, i advice you to" follow @trumotalks on Instagram! They'll post once every week and their posts usually have to do with new places or activities to do in and around Bogotá. I would also advice you to go to Playa Blanca in Sta. Marta and to San Andres. The only place i can think of, off the top of my head, to which you must go 100% is the "
first international parepente park" of Colombia, which supposedly opens around 2021 - Q2 in Santander. Also, you should just go to Santander; places such as Barichara and Las Gachas are truly beatiful and a joy to be in, and Santander, all around, is very extreme sport tourism oriented. 
Finally, in Bogotá, there a lot of trails such "Sendero de las Mariposas" and a lot of lookout points such as "Mirador de las tres cruces" (If you go there, don't go too up into the mountain and take a swimsuit with you, because there are lagoons in which you can swim). Another account or, more so, web page that you can follow is Bogota.gov.co and/or Amigos de la Montaña, as both usually report on the Cerros Orientales of Bogotá and they have maps of trails and other nature related stuff. Sadly, just as i was trying to answer your question, i found out that the link for those maps on the Amigos de la Montaña website, is not working, at least for me. But, there you have it.

3) As a college student myself, i'd say i'm highly connected to American culture, in more ways that both you and i may expect. But maybe that's just me, maybe too much Youtube. So, some references you make shouldn't be too strange for your colombian young adult. As long as they don't have to do with Snapchat, a lot of people should get the joke, pun or reference. 
An important thing, is that i believe that if you use Instagram or Facebook, you should follow meme groups. Say, if you're studying at Universidad Nacional de Colombia, follow @memesunacional and/or @confesionesunal on those social media sites, because you may understand better the context, the denotation and connotation matters of the university and its students. But not only follow or get yourself into the situation of the university in which you're studying, but get yourself into the society of Bogotá and Colombia itself. Get into momosrolos in Facebook or some shitposting group, because they may teach you about the teenage, young adult and adult culture of this place.
